chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid al-Attar, from Muhammad ibn Rashid al-Barmaki, from Umar ibn Sahl al-Asadi, from Sahl ibn Ghazwan al-Basri who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, a female jinn called Afra used to go to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), hear his words, and then go to the righteous jinn, conveying the greeting through her hand. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) missed her and asked Gabriel (peace be upon him) about her. He said: 'She has gone to visit one of her sisters whom she loves for the sake of God.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Blessed are those who love each other for the sake of God. Indeed, God, the Blessed and Exalted, has created in Paradise a pillar of red ruby, upon which are seventy thousand palaces, in each palace seventy thousand rooms, which God the Mighty and Majestic created for those who love each other and visit each other.'

O Afra, what did you see? She said: I saw many wonders. He asked: What was the most wondrous thing you saw? She said: I saw Satan in the green sea, on a white rock, stretching his hands to the sky, saying: 'O my God, when You fulfill Your promise and cast me into the Fire of Hell, I ask You by the right of Muhammad, Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan, and al-Hussein, to release me from it and resurrect me with them.' I said to him: O Satan, what are these names by which you invoke? He said to me: I saw them on the leg of the Throne, before God created Adam by seven thousand years, so I knew that they are the most honored of creation to God, so I ask Him by their right. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'By God, if the people of the earth were to swear by these names, He would answer them.'

key_terms.الْمُتَحَابِّينَ: Those who love each other (for the sake of God)
key_terms.الْمُتَزَاوِرِينَ: Those who visit each other (for the sake of God)
key_terms.بِحَقِّ: By the right of, referring to the status/authority of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.طُوبَى: Tuba, meaning blessedness or good news
key_terms.عَفْرَاءُ: Afra, the name of the female jinn in the narration
key_terms.يَاقُوتَةٍ حَمْرَاءَ: Red ruby, describing the material of the pillar in Paradise

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who love each other for the sake of God, and how does Satan seek intercession through the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to establish the pre-eternal excellence of the Ahl al-Bayt, noting that their names were inscribed on the Throne seven thousand years before Adam, a concept central to Shia cosmology. The story of Afra serves to illustrate the interconnectedness of the jinn and human realms through divine revelation, while Satan’s invocation underscores the universal authority of the Prophet and his family, affirming that their intercessory rights are potent enough to even sway the adversary.
